<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<feed xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom"><entry>
    <id>https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.10101</id>
    <title>Paged key-value caching for high-throughput transformer serving</title>
    <summary>Fragmentation in the key-value cache wastes between 20 and 40 percent of GPU memory in production serving. Allocating the cache in fixed-size pages raises achievable batch size by 2.2 times and improves throughput by 1.9 times with no change to model outputs, since the technique is numerically exact.</summary>
    <published>2024-01-18T00:00:00Z</published>
    <author><name>Barbara Liskov</name></author>
  </entry><entry>
    <id>https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.20202</id>
    <title>Speculative decoding with lightweight draft models</title>
    <summary>A small draft model proposes tokens that the target model verifies in parallel. Because verification is exact, the output distribution is unchanged. We measure wall-clock speedups of 2.1 to 2.8 times on greedy decoding, with the acceptance rate of drafted tokens being the dominant factor in the realised gain.</summary>
    <published>2024-02-29T00:00:00Z</published>
    <author><name>Edsger Dijkstra</name></author><author><name>Frances Allen</name></author>
  </entry></feed>
